title: Hair Transplant Before & After Photos: How to Spot Real vs Edited Results
seoTitle: Hair Transplant Before & After Photos: Spot Real Results
metaDescription: Spot misleading hair transplant photos, ask for 12-month daylight video, set Norwood 3 vs 5–6 density expectations, and verify independent reviews.
quickAnswer: Spotting hair transplant before and after real results requires checking for identical lighting, head tilt, dry hair styling, and uncropped donor views across both photos. Always ask for 12-month comb-through videos in natural daylight, compare cases matching your own Norwood stage, and verify reviews outside clinic-controlled social feeds.

What lighting, angle and wet-hair tricks make clinic photos misleading?

A hair transplant gallery can double perceived density without adding a single follicle. Common visual tricks include harsh overhead flash in the "before" photo paired with soft dim lighting in the "after" photo, wet or slicked-back hair before surgery versus blow-dried volume afterward, tilted chins hiding the crown, and concealing fibres.

The [British Association of Hair Restoration Surgery (BAHRS)](https://www.bahrs.co.uk/blog/top-10-tips-for-minimising-the-risk-of-hair-transplant-surgery-claims/) stresses that fair clinical comparisons require standardized head position, lighting, hair length, and styling. Meanwhile, the [ISHRS Fight the FIGHT campaign](https://fightthefight.ishrs.org/tips-to-avoid-bad-hair-transplant-clinic/) warns that unethical clinics sometimes steal before-and-after galleries from reputable physicians altogether.

body.text: Why should you ask for 12-month video results in natural daylight?

Still photos freeze a single flattering second, whereas a continuous comb-through video shot in natural daylight reveals hairline softness, graft direction, exit angles, and true see-through density in motion. Requesting 12-month (or 12- to 18-month) follow-ups matters because early 6-month photos rarely show final texture, maturation, or donor healing.

According to [NHS hair transplant guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/cosmetic-surgery/hair-transplant/), full results typically take 10 to 18 months to appear. A short handheld video where someone parts the hairline and runs a comb through the mid-scalp and donor zone under bright daylight is far harder to manipulate with filters, contrast sliders, or strategic comb-overs than a staged Instagram carousel.
What realistic density should Norwood 3 vs Norwood 5–6 patients expect?

Realistic visual density depends on your baldness stage, donor supply, hair shaft thickness, curl, and hair-to-skin contrast. A Norwood 3 patient with strong donor density can often achieve dense, natural frontal framing in one session, whereas a Norwood 5 or 6 patient has a much larger bald surface and must prioritize realistic coverage over teenage density.

The [ISHRS FUE Clinical Practice Guidelines](https://ishrs.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/July-15-2019-FUE-Guidelines.pdf) note that natural donor density typically ranges from 60 to 100 follicular units per cm², and thick or wavy hair creates a denser visual effect than fine straight hair. For advanced stages like Norwood 6, [ISHRS surgical guidance](https://ishrs.org/fut/) emphasizes that the usable safe donor area is narrower, meaning ethical surgeons plan conservative hairlines, staged sessions, or lighter crown coverage rather than overharvesting the donor zone. Review our [hair transplant risks briefing](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/hair-transplant-risks-turkey) to understand why chasing maximum single-day graft counts backfires.
How do you verify independent patient reviews?

Clinic websites and paid influencer reels rarely reflect average outcomes or complication handling. Verifying independent reviews means cross-checking multi-month patient journeys on third-party hair-loss forums, confirming the named surgeon's credentials on official directories, and checking whether the facility holds an active authorization certificate in Türkiye.
Use this verification checklist before trusting any online gallery or five-star rating:

items: Confirm the facility legally: Search the clinic's exact corporate name on the [Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Health authorized provider list](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html).

Check physician credentials: Verify named doctors via the [ISHRS Find a Doctor directory](https://ishrs.org/find-a-doctor/) and confirm who actually performs extractions and incisions, as advised by [BAHRS patient guidance](https://www.bahrs.co.uk/patient-advice/).
Look for 12-month independent threads: Prioritize patient-posted progress logs showing pre-op, immediate post-op graft placement, 6-month, and 12-month photos—not day-three hotel-lobby testimonials.
Match the specific doctor, not just the brand: Large Istanbul clinics rotate multiple teams; verify reviews name the exact physician treating you.

Keep logistics separate from marketing: Book travel and [Istanbul recovery hotels](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/hair-transplant-recovery-hotel-istanbul) independently through our [medical tourism logistics service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism) so accommodation perks never cloud clinical judgment.

faq.q: Why do so many clinics only post 6-month or immediate post-op photos?
faq.a: Immediate post-op photos show neat graft placement but prove nothing about survival rate, while 6-month shots often catch early growth before donor thinning or uneven yield becomes obvious.

faq.q: Can reverse image search detect stolen before-and-after photos?
faq.a: Yes. Running a reverse image search on a clinic's flagship gallery photos can reveal whether the same patient appears on another surgeon's website in a different country.

faq.q: Do thicker hair shafts really look denser with the same graft count?
faq.a: Yes. Per [ISHRS clinical guidelines](https://ishrs.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/08/July-15-2019-FUE-Guidelines.pdf), wider hair shaft diameter, curl, and lower hair-to-scalp colour contrast all increase perceived coverage without requiring more grafts.

faq.q: Why are day-one five-star Google reviews unreliable for hair transplants?
faq.a: A day-one review only rates airport pickup, hotel comfort, and staff friendliness. True surgical quality cannot be judged until at least 10 to 12 months later.

faq.q: What if a clinic refuses to show donor-area after photos?
faq.a: Treat that as a serious warning sign. Reputable surgeons document both recipient growth and healed donor zones transparently—otherwise patients risk facing [hair transplant repair](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/hair-transplant-repair-turkey) later.
